Life is not easy, especially when you're a dumb chicken on a planet whose entire fauna seems to consist of enormous Ssaari lizards. But the chickmunks find a way. As the old song says: “If you're gonna be dumb, you gotta be tough.”

Most encounters with a Chickmunk Alfa end the same way as a Friday night at a bar: projectile vomiting. Only, instead of tequila, whatever comes blasting from the Chickmunk’s beak is a spray of razor-sharp crystal shards, each one shaped like a tiny needle.

My first thought was convergent evolution. But then you look at her! Two eyes. Ears. Legs. Bre... I mean, everything is the right number, in exactly the right places. That’s weird. Sixties sci-fi show levels of weird! Please let it be explained by convergent evolution instead of something "more sinister"!

Steel armor, a scimitar, and an old-fashioned jetpack. Artifacts from a much more advanced era, perhaps? But I’ve got an even wilder theory. Maybe, just maybe, the technology on their world simply never evolved to be used by the masses. The more you learn about the Xenauri and especially about the Altari, the more reasonable that theory starts to sound!

Big scaly lizard with bone-breaking jaws. Except on the Xenauri planet, the big scaly lizard with bone-breaking jaws is the only kind of fauna. And those jaws aren’t for breaking bones. They’re for crushing crystals. So, not a herbivore. Carnivore is also wrong, and don’t even think about “omnivore.” The closest term is lithophagy.

Think of dinosaurs. “Clever” would hardly be your first association, right? But Screamers are surprisingly clever. Imagine a dog carrying a little barrel of rum for winter hikers in need. Only instead of booze, it carries medical supplies. That’s about the level of clever we’re talking about.

A focused mind is absolutely necessary when wielding Altari powers. But focusing amid the chaos of battle is no easy task. That’s why some Altari came up with chants. Facing danger with a song in one’s heart definitely produces better results... at least for Altari.

They channel the energy of dead soldiers through ritual chants, turning battlefield casualties into magical power. If that’s the best explanation modern science can offer, it really sucks. Give me a year, a grant, a lab, some assistants, and unlimited coffee, and I’m sure I can come up with something better.
Their staff is supposed to help them channel their Altari power. In practice, they mostly use it for pointing dramatically, hitting things, and making sure everyone knows they are definitely Altari.

Wearing the traditional Xenauri face-covering helmet can be quite practical. It protects the wearer from dust and razor-sharp crystal shards flying across the battlefield, and it can also hide an expression of absolute horror when some of your Altari tricks inevitably go wrong.

These are not your usual dumb Ssaari. Fowlers can talk! Okay, like a three-year-old, but still! Their intelligence has sparked plenty of debate about their evolution, but the biggest question remains unspoken. Is what we see today evolution, or decline? As the crystals of the Xenauri world erased traces of its ancient history, we can only guess.

Fowlers may adore their little Firebirds, but they understand just how important they are to the clan’s defense. When the heroic and honorable warriors of the clan set out on their noble missions to acquire resources, the Firebirds are all that stand between their homes and the barbaric savages of rival clans who come to murder and pillage.

One of the most ferocious predators on the Xenauri planet... but wait. Aren’t most Ssaari supposed to be lithophagous? Could those instincts be a forgotten genetic legacy from a time before everything became hard, translucent, sharp, and neatly arranged according to a Bravais lattice?

Becoming a Blood Rider is one of the few ways to come close to the martial prowess of the Altari. Not the doomsday, psyker-level Altari (they remain far beyond the reach of any ordinary Xenauri), but the everyday, run-of-the-mill Altari? Sure, why not?

One of the smallest creatures of the Xenauri planet is the little Firebird. Its ability to explode is one of the most efficient species defense mechanisms. Benefit for the individual? Zero. Benefit for the species? Beyond count.

Unification under the Pathfinder banner was far from peaceful. The crystal desert clan leader Batu did not submit, even under the threat of the Pathfinder’s Altari entering the fight. Only when the Pathfinder raised the Mothership from the desert did Batu finally believe the exodus was not just a convenient story.
Mountains are harsh on every world, but the crystal peaks of the Xenauri planet are beyond cruel. No Xenauri clan can survive there for long. None but Razak’s.

Following tradition, male Xenauri cover their faces with helmets. From that moment, it is considered to be their second face. Every scratch and dent on a helmet tells the story of a fight, and Morzai’s helmet could fill a ten-volume novel.

Usually, the Xenauri own only armor, a weapon, a coffee service, and a few necessities that can be carried around. But from all the jewelry Kiret piled up during his short "stay" in the Siren System, it is absolutely clear that Kiret was born different.

Your eyes do not deceive you! Saheru is not a Xenauri, he is a Ssaari. An exceptionally intelligent one, but still a Ssaari. Xenauri who follow him are called crazy, but everyone who stands in his shadow knows exactly whom they follow, and that mountain of muscle casts a very long shadow.

Shagat never fully aligned with the resettlement to the Siren System. As a member of the Pathfinder’s Altari Guard, he never had a choice. Now he is roaming the system, seeking a way to return to his homeworld. Maybe he is missing the old ways, or perhaps someone the exodus left behind.

When the mysterious prophet came from the crystal desert, nobody listened to his words. To leave the planet that had been the Xenauri’s home for countless generations? What a joke! But when the strongest Altari suddenly took his side, nobody laughed anymore.

Once one of the Pathfinder’s elite Altari Guard, Tengri possesses an exceptional level of psionic abilities. Despite his destructive power, he is surprisingly gentle by nature, seeking comfort in peaceful forests rather than fighting for glory.

A caravan found her among the bodies of the fallen, her armor pierced and bloodied, and took her for dead. When they tried to pry her scimitar from her hand, her fingers would not yield, holding fast as fiercely as her spirit clung to her wounded body. Months later, the caravan passed that same road again, but this time she rode at its head, commander of its guard.

All her life, technology had been the privilege of the Altari, another distant power she could only watch from afar. On her first day in the Siren System, she took a wristwatch from a dead UNSS soldier. Stunned by the simple miracle of machinery answering to her touch, she realized she had left behind not only her world, but the limits it had placed upon her.

In the no-man’s-land, her clan uncovered an ancient shelter. Inside, they found an old map showing a vast green expanse, but only Tu-Fira dared follow its uncertain guide. She found only unfamiliar crystal formations. She did not find shapes like that again until years later, when she saw the trees of the Siren System for the first time.

During her childhood, Se-Wari hated her luck. Why hadn’t she received the same gift as her Altari sister? But later, much later, she came to realize that gift was a curse in disguise. The Altari would never truly be free; their powers made them a constant target. In that moment, all her anger faded away. She would be there for her sister. Always.

When her sister Se-Tri became one of the Pathfinder’s Altari Guard, a lot changed. Se-Wari's lack of psionic powers made it hard to keep up with her gifted sister, but when the Pathfinder announced the invasion of the Siren System, Se-Wari chose to stay by her sister’s side anyway.

The young adapt when the old become obsolete. Ki-Khi has not even grown out of her children’s armor, yet the pulse rifle in her small hands is more than a weapon. It is a sign that the long decline of the masters of the blade from the crystal wastelands has only just begun.

Ra-Win had never enjoyed the attention that usually followed Altari. As she grew older, her powers surpassed those of even the strongest Altari in her clan, until the Pathfinder took notice. Now that she has left his side, she hopes the wilderness will offer her a place to disappear. But power like hers has always drawn unwanted eyes.

“Little Se-Tri is the most gifted Altari! She will bring our clan the brightest future!” But being special meant living in the spotlight, alone, admired and feared in equal measure. The only one who never feared her was her sister. Sometimes, one person is all you need.

One of the strongest Altari in the Siren System. Before she became a member of the Pathfinder's Altari Guard, Se-Tri and her twin sister Se-Wari were inseparable; now all Se-Tri cares about is her duty to the Pathfinder.

Stronger than an ordinary Altari, but not powerful enough to attract the Pathfinder’s attention, Ri-Sh found the perfect balance between power and freedom. Now, she sells her abilities to the highest bidder, and you wouldn’t believe how high the demand is.
